At Atlantic Veterinary Internal Medicine & Oncology (AVIM&O), we offer advanced oncologic treatment options designed to help pets live life to the fullest, always prioritizing their quality of life in every recommendation. Our chemotherapy and oncology services go beyond just treating cancer—they also focus on diagnosing, preventing, and researching it. We stay on the cutting edge of veterinary medicine, using the latest knowledge, protocols, and treatments to fully understand and manage your pet’s cancer journey.
Our board-certified, residency-trained team of oncologists is committed to providing compassionate, state-of-the-art care. We will work closely with you to carefully discuss all available treatment options and guide you in choosing the best approach for your pet’s unique needs.
Oncology Consultations
Our veterinary oncology consultations are the cornerstone of the care we provide. During the consultation, we will carefully review your pet's medical records, gather valuable insights from your observations, and take the time to understand your goals and concerns. A thorough physical examination will also be performed to assess your pet's condition.
We take the time to understand your pet’s unique needs so we can recommend the best diagnostic and treatment options to help them feel better, faster. We will discuss the prognosis for your pet and provide a detailed estimate of the financial costs, ensuring transparency and clarity.
Our doctors and staff are here for you every step of the way, working hand-in-hand with you and your primary care veterinarian to support you in making the best decisions for your beloved companion.
To support you in making informed decisions, we work closely with you and your primary care veterinarian every step of the way.

Chemotherapy
Before starting treatment, we will take a detailed medical history and assess your pet’s current condition. A comprehensive physical exam will be performed, followed by a thorough review of diagnostic and treatment options.
During your consultation, we will discuss the risks and benefits of chemotherapy in detail, ensuring you feel informed and confident in the treatment plan. The recommended chemotherapy, whether injectable or oral, will be tailored to your pet’s specific cancer type and overall health. Unlike in human medicine, chemotherapy for dogs and cats is carefully designed to minimize side effects, prioritizing their comfort and well-being. Your pet’s quality of life is always our top priority, and we are committed to providing compassionate care every step of the way.
Throughout treatment, ongoing tests and monitoring may be necessary to track progress and adjust care as needed. This may include blood work, imaging such as X-rays, ultrasounds, or CT scans, and regular reassessments. We work closely with pet owners and referring veterinarians, collaborating at every stage to achieve the best possible outcome for your beloved companion.
Electrochemotherapy
What Is Electrochemotherapy?
Electrochemotherapy (ECT) is an advanced cancer treatment option offered at our Hunt Valley location that enhances the effectiveness of traditional chemotherapy for certain tumors. This technique combines chemotherapy drugs with the local application of short, controlled electric pulses. The pulses temporarily increase the permeability of cancer cell membranes, allowing the chemotherapy to enter the cells far more efficiently, up to thousands of times greater than with standard intravenous (IV) administration alone.
While surgery, radiation therapy, chemotherapy, or a combination of these treatments remain the gold standard for managing solid tumors and incomplete surgical margins, electrochemotherapy can be a safe and effective adjunct or alternative in select cases. Its targeted approach, relative affordability, and minimally invasive nature make ECT a valuable addition to the range of oncology therapies available for pets.
